newsitem.title: USA: Donnkenny hits year low as auditors resign.
newsitem.headline: Donnkenny hits year low as auditors resign.

text.p: Women's sportswear maker Donnkenny Inc's shares dropped 3-5/8 to a new 52-week low of 8-7/8 as news that the company's auditors resigned spooked investors.
Late on Wednesday, Donnkenny said KPMG Peat Marwick resigned and had been replaced by Deloitte and Touche LLP. Donnkenny has yet to comment on the reason for the resignation.
The firm also said Stewart Levy replaced Ed Creevy as chief financial officer. The company said it had not yet detemined whether Creevy will remain with the company.

"You have a company with a credibility problem. The write-down last year, the chairman selling stock, and now the auditors resigning scared the hell out of everybody," said Steve Schneider, an analyst with St. Louis-based Stifel Nicolaus.
Early on Thursday, Schneider suspended his buy rating on Donnkenny, but reinstated a long-term buy rating after speaking with the company.
Although Donnkenny declined to comment on the reason for the auditors' resignation, Schneider said the company told analysts that there was no fraud involved.
Donnkenny also told analysts that it expects its earnings to fall within analysts' range of estimates.
Schneider said he expects Donnkenny to earn about $1.34 a share for fiscal 1996, slightly below Wall Street's consensus estimate of $1.36 a share.
Schneider said he expects Donnkenny's share price to rebound after it reports third quarter financial results next week.
"The stock will be up significanly by the time their numbers come out and things are more clear," Schneider said.
Earlier on Thursday, Rodman & Renshaw cut Donnkenny to neutral from buy, and Bear Stearns downgraded it to neutral from attractive.
